title: Herz versus Fefferman: Symmetric and asymmetric Bochner--Riesz theory
summary: We study Bochner--Riesz summability for a one-dimensional model of noncompact manifolds with ends. Each end has an effective Euclidean dimension, and these dimensions may differ from one end to another. The central point is the contrast between the symmetric and asymmetric cases. When the end dimensions agree, the model follows Herz's radial theory for the Euclidean Laplacian. When they are unequal, a Fefferman-type obstruction appears, analogous to the ball multiplier obstruction in higher-dimensional Fourier analysis, even though the model itself is one-dimensional.
